title: Elysia team invitations
context: Team invitations. Only team admins create invites. An invite joins the team it was created for, may be accepted once, only by the user whose email it was sent to (emails compare case-insensitively), and only before expires_at (a Date). `db` is a pg-promise client; `tx` runs its callback in a transaction.
code: export const invites = new Elysia({ prefix: "/teams/:teamId/invites" })
const member = await db.oneOrNone("SELECT role FROM memberships WHERE team_id = $1 AND user_id = $2", [params.teamId, currentUser.id]);
await db.none("INSERT INTO invites (token, team_id, email, expires_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)", [token, params.teamId, body.email, expiresAt]);
const invite = await db.oneOrNone("SELECT * FROM invites WHERE token = $1", [params.token]);
await tx.none("INSERT INTO memberships (team_id, user_id, role) VALUES ($1, $2, 'member')", [params.teamId, currentUser.id]);
await tx.none("UPDATE invites SET accepted_at = now() WHERE token = $1", [params.token]);

expected.why: lookup ignores team_id, so a valid invite for one team can be used to join any :teamId in the URL
emails must compare case-insensitively; a different-case address is wrongly refused
accepted_at is checked outside the transaction and this update has no AND accepted_at IS NULL / row-count check, so parallel accepts all succeed
